discovery: Prediction and discovery of flat bands, correlated insulators and superconductivity in magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene

nominees.name: Allan H. MacDonald
nominees.affiliation: University of Texas at Austin, USA

subfield: Condensed matter physics: quantum materials / moiré systems
motivation: In 2011 Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted that at a 'magic' twist angle near 1.1 degrees, the Dirac bands of bilayer graphene become nearly flat, so that interactions dominate the kinetic energy. In 2018 Jarillo-Herrero's group realized this prediction, discovering correlated insulating states and unconventional superconductivity that can be tuned with a gate voltage in a single device. This work created moiré quantum matter, a whole new materials platform. Twist angle became a design parameter, and strong correlations and band topology could be combined at will. The field it launched has since produced orbital ferromagnetism, the quantized anomalous Hall effect, and fractional Chern insulators at zero magnetic field in moiré graphene and transition-metal dichalcogenides. Few recent advances have so completely changed what condensed matter physicists look for and how they build quantum phases. This is a clear case of a concrete theoretical prediction followed by a decisive experimental discovery.
